title: Gamaliel's advice (Acts 5:12–42)
hookLine: if it's from God, you won't be able to stop it
tomorrow: the church grows, and some widows get missed at dinner. who notices?

lines: THE ONE WHO SAYS, WAIT A DAY.
cards: Some group chats have one person who says, let's wait a day, while everyone else is furious. Acts 5 has that person.
The apostles stand before the council again, and Peter's answer is short: "We ought to obey God rather than men." The room is enraged; Acts says they took counsel to slay them.
Then one man stands up: "a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people." And what he says is: let them alone.

teach.b: He has the apostles put outside for a little while and speaks to the council. Take care, he says, what you mean to do.
He reminds them of movements that rose before, Theudas and Judas of Galilee; each gathered followers, and each came to nothing.

Then his advice: "Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God."
Notice who the calm voice is: a Pharisee, a teacher of the law, honored by the people. The council takes his advice, partly.

They still have the apostles beaten and order them not to speak in Jesus' name, then let them go. And the apostles leave "rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name." Gamaliel's test is patient.
It isn't indifference; he warns about fighting against God. It isn't approval either; Acts never says he joined them. It's humility about how much one angry room can know in one afternoon.
One to tell a friend tonight: later in Acts, Paul says he was brought up "at the feet of Gamaliel."
The teacher who said wait had a student who would turn the whole story.

how: Some Christians quote Gamaliel's 'if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it' when a new idea or movement divides a congregation, as a reason to wait before opposing it.

o: wait and see before you oppose something
defend new ideas no matter what it costs
always side with the majority in a room

games.q: the calm voice — tap the pairs.
p: we ought to obey God rather than men
a Pharisee, a doctor of the law
an earlier movement that came to nothing

s: the Pharisees in Acts are always the villains
Gamaliel, a Pharisee and doctor of the law, is the calm voice whose advice the council takes.
Gamaliel joins the apostles after his speech
Acts doesn't say so. he only says: let them alone, and wait.
the apostles left the council rejoicing
rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.

games.q: a new hire at work suggests a whole new way to run the weekly meeting. your gut says it won't work. what's Gamaliel's way?
o: let it run for a few weeks and see what lasts.
shut it down now, before it wastes everyone's time.
back it fully, since new ideas deserve a yes.
games.why: if this counsel be of men, it will come to nought: but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it. Gamaliel trusted time to sort it.

practice: Stand and walk slowly, a few steps and back, for about a minute. With each step, hold one thing you're ready to oppose: a plan, an idea, someone's suggestion.
Don't decide; let the steps give it time, then sit and breathe with whatever is left.

wordCard.voice: Gamaliel's advice. Let them alone: if it's only human, it will fade; if it's from God, you can't stop it.
